title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
description: Given the head of a linked list and an integer `n`, delete the `n`-th node counting from the **end** of the list (so `n = 1` is the last node) and return the head of the resulting list. Try to do it in a single pass.
hints: Counting the length first and then walking again works in two passes. Can you find the target in one?
If one pointer is exactly n nodes ahead of another, what is true about the second pointer when the first reaches the end?
Use a dummy node before the head (handles removing the head). Advance a lead pointer n steps, then move lead and a trailing pointer together until lead.next is None. Trail.next is the node to skip.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def removeNthFromEnd(self, head: Optional[ListNode], n: int) -> Optional[ListNode]:

solution.explanation: Put a dummy node in front of the head so removing the first node is not a special case. Send a lead pointer n steps ahead, then advance lead and a trailing pointer (starting at the dummy) together until lead reaches the last node. The trailing pointer is now just before the node to delete, so link it past that node. One pass: O(L) time, O(1) space.
